# ThaiData UK
> UK Thai restaurant directory and market data — 1,267 FSA-listed venues across 255 cities. Restaurant pages, data reports, recipes and free owner tools. No signup.

UK Thai food industry data sourced from the Food Standards Agency (FSA), ONS, and HMRC. Updated October 2026.

## Tools
- [NLW Impact Calculator](https://thaidata.uk/): Calculate your April 2026 minimum wage cost increase in 60 seconds. Models all age tiers (21+, 18–20, apprentice) with NI and Employment Allowance.
- [Profit Margin Defender](https://thaidata.uk/tools/PROFIT_MARGIN_DEFENDER.html): Model delivery platform fees (Uber Eats 30%, Deliveroo 32%, Just Eat 14%) against your dish costs. See true per-dish net profit.
- [Chef Visa Assistant](https://thaidata.uk/tools/VISA_ASSISTANT.html): Check 2026 Skilled Worker visa eligibility for sponsoring a Thai chef. Factors the £38,700 salary threshold and sponsorship costs.
- [Wholesale Benchmarker](https://thaidata.uk/tools/WHOLESALE_BENCHMARKER.html): Compare your ingredient costs against regional UK averages for rice, oil, proteins, and Thai-specific ingredients.
- [Resilience Dashboard](https://thaidata.uk/tools/RESILIENCE_DASHBOARD.html): Predictive stress-testing for restaurant survival through NLW increases and cost pressure modeling.
- [City Opportunity Scorer](https://thaidata.uk/tools/where-to-open-thai-restaurant-uk.html): Score every UK city for Thai restaurant potential. Adjust for competition tolerance, budget, and market gap.
- [Hygiene Lookup](https://thaidata.uk/tools/thai-restaurant-hygiene-lookup.html): Search any UK Thai restaurant's FSA hygiene rating. Free, instant.
- [NAP Trust Checker](https://thaidata.uk/tools/NAP_CHECKER.html): Verify your restaurant's Name, Address, Phone consistency across Google, Yelp, and 50+ directories for AI search visibility.
- [Staffing Calculator](https://thaidata.uk/tools/thai-restaurant-staffing-calculator.html): Model headcount requirements and staff costs for different restaurant sizes.

## Core Guides
- [How to Open a Thai Restaurant in the UK](https://thaidata.uk/open-thai-restaurant-uk.html): Complete 15-step roadmap. Real costs (£80k–£180k), chef visa requirements, kitchen design for wok cooking, supplier directory.
- [UK Thai Restaurant Count](https://thaidata.uk/how-many-thai-restaurants-uk.html): 1,267 FSA-listed Thai businesses. Full regional and city breakdown. Dine-in vs takeaway splits. Updated weekly.
- [Menu Pricing Guide](https://thaidata.uk/thai-restaurant-menu-pricing-uk.html): 20-dish benchmark with food costs, London vs regional pricing, and GP targets for every major Thai dish.
- [Operating Costs](https://thaidata.uk/thai-restaurant-costs-uk.html): Real numbers on food costs, staffing (NLW 2026), rent, energy, and hidden expenses for UK Thai restaurants.
- [Delivery Commissions](https://thaidata.uk/thai-restaurant-delivery-commissions-uk.html): Platform-by-platform breakdown of Deliveroo, Uber Eats, and Just Eat fees. True margin after commission, VAT, and packaging.
- [Wholesale Suppliers](https://thaidata.uk/thai-wholesale-suppliers-uk.html): Complete directory of UK Thai-specific wholesalers. Regional coverage, minimum orders, specialty items.

## Learn
- [Thai Food Culture](https://thaidata.uk/learn): Regional differences, UK vs Thailand, health, eating patterns, and the tradition of sharing Thai dishes.

## Industry Reports
- [State of UK Thai Food 2026](https://thaidata.uk/state-of-uk-thai-food-2026.html): Definitive annual report. Market size, trends, growth rates, and competitive landscape.
- [The 2026 Chef Visa Cliff](https://thaidata.uk/analysis/chef-visa-cliff.html): Analysis of the Skilled Worker visa impact on Thai restaurant staffing. Why sponsorship routes are narrowing.
- [Revenue Benchmarks](https://thaidata.uk/thai-restaurant-revenue-benchmarks-uk.html): Real revenue and profit numbers from UK Thai restaurants. By size, location, and business model.
- [Food Trends 2026](https://thaidata.uk/thai-food-trends-uk-2026.html): What UK diners want. Regional cuisine trends, pricing sensitivity, and delivery vs dine-in shifts.

## Recipes
- [Thai Recipes Hub](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/): Real Thai recipes researched from Thai-language sources, translated and cited.
- [Khao Soi (ข้าวซอย)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-soi/): Northern Thai curry noodle soup — the authentic version, with 6 cited Thai sources.
- [Som Tum Thai (ส้มตำไทย)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/som-tum-thai/): The classic green papaya salad from a Michelin-recommended som tum chef, with the som tum family mapped.
- [Pad Krapow (ผัดกะเพรา)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-krapow/): The real holy-basil stir-fry from a Michelin-starred chef, plus the 1968 original recipe.
- [Thai Green Curry (แกงเขียวหวาน)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/green-curry/): From-scratch paste from a Michelin-starred chef, cracked coconut cream, the real green colour.
- [Tom Yum Goong (ต้มยำกุ้ง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tom-yum-goong/): The real clear hot-and-sour prawn soup — lime off the heat, prawn-head stock.
- [Laab (ลาบ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/laab/): The real Isaan minced meat salad — khao khua toasted rice powder, fresh herbs, Bib Gourmand technique.
- [Pad Thai (ผัดไทย)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-thai/): Tamarind-palm-sugar-fish-sauce balance, sen chan noodles, no ketchup — plus the 3-star Chaiya variant.
- [Massaman (แกงมัสมั่น)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/massaman/): The world's #1 curry — 16-ingredient spice paste, peanuts as a finish never a sauce.
- [Tom Kha Gai (ต้มข่าไก่)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tom-kha-gai/): Galangal coconut soup — lime off the heat, no dairy, no ginger.
- [Khao Man Gai (ข้าวมันไก่)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-man-gai/): Thai chicken rice — chicken-fat rice, tao jiao dipping sauce, three countries documented.
- [Panang (พะแนง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/panang/): The world's #1 stew — court recipe, nine-spice paste, peanuts in the curry, no lime.
- [Pad See Ew (ผัดซีอิ๊ว)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-see-ew/): Wide rice noodles charred in the wok, ice-water pork marinade, the burnt edges are the point.
- [Khao Pad (ข้าวผัด)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-pad/): Day-old rice fried hard, tomato folded in gently, prik nam pla on the side — plus the Michelin crab version.
- [Mango Sticky Rice (ข้าวเหนียวมะม่วง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/mango-sticky-rice/): Steamed glutinous rice folded with salted coconut cream — the Coachella dessert, the salt is the dish.
- [Gaeng Som (แกงส้ม)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/gaeng-som/): The sour curry with no orange — prawn meat in the paste, tamarind + lime, C-curl prawns.
- [Khao Kha Mu (ข้าวขาหมู)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-kha-mu/): Braised pork leg rice — caramel first, overnight rest, the dish that's better tomorrow.
- [Yum Neua (ยำเนื้อย่าง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/yum-neua/): Grilled beef salad — warm beef, balanced dressing, the bitter-lime lesson.
- [Tom Yum Noodle Soup (ก๋วยเตี๋ยวต้มยำ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tom-yum-noodle-soup/): Clear stock, per-bowl peanut dressing, just enough liquid to coat — not a soup.
- [Thai Iced Tea (ชาไทย)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/thai-iced-tea/): Spiced black tea, condensed milk, the layered pour — and why it's orange.
- [Red Curry (แกงเผ็ด)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/red-curry/): The curry named for being spicy — dried-chilli paste, cracked coconut cream, pork and aubergines, basil and kaffir lime to finish.
- [Pad Kee Mao (ผัดขี้เมา)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-kee-mao/): The noodles named for a drunk — pounded chilli relish, wide noodles, holy basil, fresh green peppercorns. No alcohol in the wok.
- [Chicken Satay (ไก่สะเต๊ะ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/chicken-satay/): Coconut-milk marinade, basted on the grill, peanut sauce on two curry pastes — and the ajad that cuts it.
- [Thai Fish Cakes (ทอดมันปลา)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/thai-fish-cakes/): Fish kneaded with red curry paste and kaffir lime until it bounces — the ajad pickle, not sweet chilli.
- [Thai Iced Coffee (กาแฟเย็น)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/thai-iced-coffee/): The sock-brewed coffee of the old cafés — condensed milk in the glass, evaporated milk over full ice.
- [Tab Tim Grob (ทับทิมกรอบ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tab-tim-grob/): Crisp rubies — water chestnuts in a tapioca shell, shocked in ice, under salted coconut cream.
- [Yellow Curry (แกงกะหรี่)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/yellow-curry/): The curry that runs on curry powder — chicken, potato, bay leaf, coconut milk, and ajad on the side.
- [Pad Prik King (ผัดพริกขิง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-prik-king/): The stir-fry named for its ginger — crispy pork belly, chilli-ginger paste, long beans, hair-thin kaffir lime.
- [Thai Banana Fritters (กล้วยแขก)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/thai-banana-fritters/): The fritters of the street vendors — nam wah bananas, rice-flour batter, coconut, sesame, pandan in the oil.
- [Kanom Krok (ขนมครก)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/kanom-krok/): The pancakes of the sizzling pan — rice-flour batter with cooked rice and lime water, coconut cream on top, crisp shell and custard heart.
- [Thai Omelette (ไข่เจียว)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/thai-omelette/): The omelette that must puff — eggs whisked to a froth, fried crisp-edged in hot oil, over rice with prik nam pla.
- [Nam Tok (น้ำตก)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/nam-tok/): The salad named for the waterfall — grilled pork neck dressed warm in its own juices with lime, fish sauce, toasted rice and mint.
- [Moo Ping (หมูปิ้ง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/moo-ping/): The breakfast skewers — thin pork in coriander-root and coconut marinade, charcoal-grilled and basted, with jaew.
- [Kanom Tuay (ขนมถ้วย)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/kanom-tuay/): The dessert in little cups — palm sugar and pandan custard under salted coconut cream, steamed and eaten warm.
- [Shrimp Cakes (ทอดมันกุ้ง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/shrimp-cakes/): The shrimp cakes that bounce — pounded, kneaded, crumbed and fried golden, served with ajad or plum sauce.
- [Thai Spring Rolls (ปอเปี๊ยะทอด)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/thai-spring-rolls/): The rolls that must not burst — glass noodles and pork in thin pastry, egg-sealed and fried, dipped in plum sauce.
- [Gaeng Jued (แกงจืด)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/gaeng-jued/): The soup with no chilli — clear broth, pork balls, glass noodles, tofu and toasted seaweed.
- [Cashew Chicken (ไก่ผัดเม็ดมะม่วงหิมพานต์)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/cashew-chicken/): The Chinese-Thai restaurant classic — fried chicken, roasted cashews, fried dried chillies, oyster-sauce gloss.
- [Pad Pak Bung Fai Daeng (ผัดผักบุ้งไฟแดง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-pak-bung/): The thirty-second dish — morning glory in a screaming wok with garlic, chillies and tao jiao.
- [Tom Saap (ต้มแซ่บ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tom-saap/): Isaan pork-rib soup — galangal, lemongrass and kaffir lime, soured hard, toasted rice on top.
- [Khao Tom (ข้าวต้ม)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-tom/): The breakfast rice soup — pork and crisp fried garlic over bloomed rice.
- [Hoy Tod (หอยทอด)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/hoy-tod/): The crisp-edged mussel pancake — three flours, egg, bean sprouts.
- [Yum Woon Sen (ยำวุ้นเส้น)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/yum-woon-sen/): Glass noodle salad with lime, fish sauce, fried peanuts and dried shrimp.
- [Pad Kana Moo Krob (คะน้าหมูกรอบ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-kana-moo-krob/): Chinese broccoli and crispy pork belly, the ahan tam sang classic.
- [Thai Lemon Iced Tea (ชามะนาว)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/thai-lemon-iced-tea/): Thai tea with fresh lime over ice — cha yen without the milk.
- [Rad Na (ราดหน้า)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/rad-na/): Charred wide rice noodles under silky pork gravy with tao jiao.
- [Bamee Moo Daeng (บะหมี่หมูแดง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/bamee-moo-daeng/): Yellow egg noodles with lacquered red roast pork and wontons.
- [Khao Mok Gai (ข้าวหมกไก่)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-mok-gai/): Thai-Muslim chicken biryani — yogurt marinade, butter, turmeric rice.
- [Gai Tod Hat Yai (ไก่ทอดหาดใหญ่)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/gai-tod-hat-yai/): Southern fried chicken with toasted spices and fried shallots.
- [Nom Yen (นมเย็น)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/nom-yen/): The pink milk — sala syrup, condensed milk, ice.
- [Bua Loy (บัวลอย)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/bua-loy/): Glutinous-rice balls in salted-sweet coconut milk.
- [Khao Khluk Kapi (ข้าวคลุกกะปิ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-khluk-kapi/): Shrimp-paste rice with sweet pork and a ring of sides.
- [Som Tum Pu Pla Ra (ส้มตำปูปลาร้า)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/som-tum-pu-pla-ra/): The full-Isaan papaya salad — crab, boiled pla ra.
- [Yen Ta Fo (เย็นตาโฟ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/yen-ta-fo/): The pink noodle soup — fermented tofu sauce, crisp squid.
- [Son-in-Law Eggs (ไข่ลูกเขย)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/son-in-law-eggs/): Fried boiled eggs in sweet-sour tamarind sauce.
- [Khao Na Pet (ข้าวหน้าเป็ด)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khao-na-pet/): Five-spice duck over rice with duck-drippings gravy.
- [Oliang (โอเลี้ยง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/oliang/): Thai iced black coffee from grain-roasted beans.
- [Guay Tiew Ruea (ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/guay-tiew-ruea/): Boat noodles — dark spice broth, blood, pork and crackling.
- [Gaeng Pa (แกงป่า)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/gaeng-pa/): Jungle curry — water-based, no coconut milk, green peppercorns.
- [Pad Khing (ผัดขิง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-khing/): Ginger chicken with wood-ear and tao jiao.
- [Pad Cha (ผัดฉ่า)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/pad-cha/): Fingerroot, green peppercorn and kaffir seafood stir-fry.
- [Lod Chong (ลอดช่อง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/lod-chong/): Pandan strands in sweet coconut milk.

- [Hor Mok (ห่อหมก)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/hor-mok/): Hor mok (ห่อหมก): minced fish and red curry paste set with egg and steamed in banana-leaf cups, capped with split coconut cream. Thai sources cited.
- [Kor Moo Yang (คอหมูย่าง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/kor-moo-yang/): Kor moo yang (คอหมูย่าง): marbled pork neck marinated and grilled over charcoal, sliced and dunked in nam jim jaew. Thai sources cited.
- [Yam Khai Dao (ยำไข่ดาว)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/yam-khai-dao/): Yam khai dao (ยำไข่ดาว): crispy fried eggs tossed in a tangy sweet-sour dressing with chillies, shallots and fresh vegetables — the humble fried egg as Thai salad. Thai sources cited.
- [Laab Mu Kua (ลาบหมูคั่ว)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/laab-mu-kua/): Laab mu kua (ลาบหมูคั่ว): northern Thai stir-fried laab — ground pork dry-fried with aromatic spices like galangal and long pepper, fully cooked unlike raw Isaan laab. Thai sources cited.
- [Kaeng Tai Pla (แกงไตปลา)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/kaeng-tai-pla/): Kaeng tai pla (แกงไตปลา): the south's fermented fish curry — strained tai pla broth, fresh pounded paste, grilled fish and vegetables. Thai sources cited.
- [Cha Dum Yen (ชาดำเย็น)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/cha-dum-yen/):
- [Tom Yum Pla (ต้มยำปลา)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tom-yum-pla/): Tom yum pla (ต้มยำปลา): Thai hot and sour fish soup — herbs boiled hard, fish dropped in at a rolling boil and never stirred, lime squeezed in off the heat. Thai sources cited.
- [Tom Jeud Tao Hu (ต้มจืดเต้าหู้หมูสับ)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tom-jeud-tao-hu/): Tom jeud tao hu (ต้มจืดเต้าหู้หมูสับ): Thai clear soup of pork balls kneaded with ice-cold water, shiitake soaking water for sweetness, and silky egg tofu added last. Thai sources cited.
- [Tom Luad Mu (ต้มเลือดหมู)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/tom-luad-mu/): Tom luad mu (ต้มเลือดหมู): Thai pork blood soup — clear bone broth, blood and offal blanched to order, never one-pot boiled, greens only in the last minutes. Thai sources cited.
- [Khanom Chan (ขนมชั้น)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/khanom-chan/): Khanom chan (ขนมชั้น): Thai layered pandan cake — three flours kneaded into coconut milk, steamed one thin layer at a time, nine layers for luck. Thai sources cited.
- [Nam Manao (น้ำมะนาว)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/nam-manao/): Nam manao (น้ำมะนาว): Thai lime juice — limes rolled hard and squeezed, a cooled sugar syrup, ice-cold water and the street-stall pinch of salt. Thai sources cited.
- [Nam Phrik Kha (น้ำพริกข่า)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/nam-phrik-kha/):
- [Po Pia Sot (ปอเปี๊ยะสด)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/po-pia-sot/): Po Pia Sot (ปอเปี๊ยะสด): fresh wheat spring rolls packed with five-spice stewed tofu, kun chiang sausage and egg, drenched in thick sweet-sour pa-lo sauce. Thai sources cited.
- [Sai Krok Isan (ไส้กรอกอีสาน)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/sai-krok-isan/): Sai Krok Isan (ไส้กรอกอีสาน): the northeast's lactic-fermented pork sausage with rice, garlic and pepper — hung until properly sour, grilled low over charcoal. Thai sources cited.
- [Kaeng Khae (แกงแค)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/kaeng-khae/): Kaeng khae (แกงแค): northern Thailand's greens curry — laab-style paste with makwaen, pla ra in some houses, and the garden's many vegetables. Thai sources cited.
- [Kaeng Luang (แกงเหลือง)](https://thaidata.uk/recipes/kaeng-luang/): Kaeng luang (แกงเหลือง): the south's yellow sour curry — turmeric and chillies pounded into a paste, garcinia or tamarind sour, fish added last. Thai sources cited.

Cha dum yen (ชาดำเย็น): strong Thai tea pulled through a cloth filter, sweetened and poured over ice — no milk, the street cart's dark glass. Thai sources cited. Nam jim jaew (น้ำจิ้มแจ่ว): Isaan toasted-rice dipping sauce for grilled meat — fish sauce, tamarind, lime, chilli. Thai sources cited. Nam Bai Toey (น้ำใบเตย) — Thai pandan drink: pandan leaves simmered in water until it changes colour, sweetened with sugar and a pinch of salt, served over ice. Home version from Kapook; variations from PROUD, Wongnai and KRUA.CO. Khao Yam (ข้าวยำ) — southern Thai rice salad: shredded herbs, roasted coconut, pounded dried shrimp and butterfly-pea rice dressed with simmered budu sauce. Thai sources cited. Khanom Jeen Nam Ngiao (ขนมจีนน้ำเงี้ยว) — northern Thai tomato-and-pork rice noodle curry with thua nao, ngiao flowers and optional blood cubes. Thai sources cited. Pad Sator (ผัดสะตอ) — southern Thai stir-fry of sataw (stink) beans with shrimp paste, bird's eye chillies, minced pork and prawns; beans tossed in last, lime squeezed over off the heat. Home version from Wongnai; variations from Mahidol INMU, Pim, SiamKapi, Foodland. Tom klong (ต้มโคล้ง): smoked-fish sour soup with dry-roasted galangal, lemongrass and tamarind. Thai sources cited. Nam Phrik Pla Too (น้ำพริกปลาทู) — Thai mackerel chilli dip. Mackerel grilled, fried or steamed, boned and pounded with char-roasted garlic, shallots and bird's eye chillies, seasoned with lime juice, fish sauce and palm sugar. Pla ra, dry-stir-fried and canned-tuna versions documented. Thai sources cited. Nam Phrik Kapi (น้ำพริกกะปิ) — Thai shrimp paste chilli dip. Chillies, garlic and banana-leaf-grilled shrimp paste pounded with palm sugar, lime juice and fish sauce, served with vegetables, fried mackerel and cha-om omelette. Ancient orange-juice, thick no-water, quick and tamarind versions documented. Thai sources cited. Nam dok anchan (น้ำดอกอัญชัน): Thai butterfly pea flower drink — boiled petals, sugar, ice, and the lime squeeze that turns it purple. Thai sources cited. Kaeng hang lay (แกงฮังเล): northern Thai Burmese-style pork curry — belly and neck marinated in a ginger-garlic paste, slow-simmered with tamarind, no coconut milk. Thai sources cited. Yam Som O (ยำส้มโอ) — Thai pomelo salad: pomelo segments tossed with roasted coconut, dried shrimp and fried shallots in a palm-sugar-tamarind coconut-cream dressing. Thai sources cited. Pla Goong (พล่ากุ้ง) — Thai prawn spicy salad: blanched prawns tossed with fine-sliced lemongrass, makrut leaf, mint and a lime-chilli dressing. Thai sources cited. Nam Phrik Num (น้ำพริกหนุ่ม) — Northern Thai grilled green chilli dip. Phrik num chillies, Thai shallots and garlic charred over a low fire, peeled and pounded coarse with salt. Lime-and-fish-sauce, pla ra and roasted-aubergine versions documented. Thai sources cited. Nam Phrik Ong (น้ำพริกอ่อง) — Northern Thai tomato and minced pork chilli dip. Dried-chilli paste pounded with shallots, garlic and shrimp paste, fried with fatty minced pork and tomatoes until the tomato collapses. Thua nao, tao jiao and red-curry-paste variants documented. Thai sources cited. Khao Mun Gai Tod (ข้าวมันไก่ทอด) — fried-chicken Thai chicken rice: garlic-ginger chicken-fat rice under crisp battered chicken with sweet chilli sauce. Thai sources cited. Gaeng Om (แกงอ่อม) — Isaan herbal stew of chicken, pla ra, lemongrass, dill and toasted rice; the curry without coconut. Thai sources cited. Kaeng Kua Gai (แกงคั่วไก่) — chicken fried in a spice-free red curry paste with coconut cream until the oil splits, simmered dry with winter melon. Three regional versions documented. Thai sources cited. Miang kham (เมี่ยงคำ): Thai betel leaf wraps with palm-sugar shrimp-paste sauce, home version from ReadTheCloud, five more Thai sources cited. ## City Data
- [London](https://thaidata.uk/cities/london.html): 280 Thai businesses. Per-capita density, hygiene ratings, dine-in/takeaway split.
- [Leeds](https://thaidata.uk/cities/leeds.html): 27 Thai businesses, ★4.4 avg rating, 4.2/100k density.
- [Manchester](https://thaidata.uk/cities/manchester.html): 19 Thai businesses, ★4.1 avg rating, 4.9/100k density.
- [Edinburgh](https://thaidata.uk/cities/edinburgh.html): 20 Thai businesses, ★4.2 avg rating, 4.4/100k density.
- [Bristol](https://thaidata.uk/cities/bristol.html): 14 Thai businesses, ★4.6 avg rating.
- [Birmingham](https://thaidata.uk/cities/birmingham.html): 8 Thai businesses, ★4.4 avg rating, 1.5/100k (underserved).
- [All 15 cities](https://thaidata.uk/thai-restaurants-city-breakdown-uk.html): Full city-by-city comparison table with 78 UK cities analyzed.
- [City Scorer Tool](https://thaidata.uk/tools/where-to-open-thai-restaurant-uk.html): Interactive tool. Weight population, competition, costs. Find your best city.

## Events
- [Festival Calendar](https://thaidata.uk/thai-festivals-uk.html): Complete UK Thai events calendar. Songkran, Loy Krathong, food festivals, temple celebrations.
- [Songkran 2026](https://thaidata.uk/songkran-uk.html): Thai New Year events across the UK. Dates, venues, traditions.
- [Loy Krathong](https://thaidata.uk/loy-krathong-uk.html): Festival of Lights. UK celebrations, locations, dates.

## Chains
- [UK Thai Restaurant Chains](https://thaidata.uk/thai-chains-uk): Data comparison of 10 UK Thai chains. Location counts, FSA hygiene ratings, geographic coverage. Giggling Squid (47), Rosa's Thai (39), Busaba (7), and more.

## Data
- [Hugging Face Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/thaidata/uk-thai-restaurants): Full dataset — FSA records including historical and delisted venues, geocoded. Free to use (ODbL).
- [API](https://thaidata.uk/api/v1/): Machine-readable JSON endpoint for UK Thai restaurant statistics.
- [MCP Server](https://thaidata.uk/mcp): Model Context Protocol endpoint — AI agents can query ThaiData directly as a tool. 8 query functions.
- [Site Map](https://thaidata.uk/sitemap-page): Full HTML site map of all pages.
- [About](https://thaidata.uk/about): About ThaiData UK. Data methodology and sources.
- [Data Quality](https://thaidata.uk/data-quality): Full methodology, source attribution, update schedule, and trust signals.
